(p-٣٤٠٧)In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

Surat Hud

It is ascribed to him (Hud) because it contains his story with his people, and to distinguish it, although it also contains the accounts of other prophets, peace be upon them.

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named after His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ [Hud: 56], which indicates the oneness of actions, together with its uprightness in giving each capable one what it is prepared for, which entails the rulings and the recompense, and these are among the greatest of purposes. End quote.

It is Meccan. Three verses are excepted from it, which were revealed in Medina and were attached to it: ﴿So perhaps you will leave [some] of what is revealed to you﴾ [Hud: 12], ﴿Then is one who had clear evidence from his Lord﴾ [Hud: 17], and ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ [Hud: 114].

Its verses number one hundred and twenty-three.

Al-Hakim narrated, "From Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: O Messenger of God! You have grown gray! He said: Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'aluna, and 'Idha al-shamsu kuwwirat have made me gray." He and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abbas.

It is also narrated from Anas, Sahl, and Imran. In one narration: "Hud and its sisters, the mention of the Day of Resurrection and the stories of the nations, have made me gray."

In another narration: "Hud and its sisters have made me gray, and what was done to the nations."

(p-٣٤٠٨)In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful

The discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[1] ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been perfected and then presented in detail from One who is Wise and Acquainted.﴾

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ The discussion of similar letters has preceded at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, so let it be recalled.

﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected﴾ meaning: they were arranged in a firm, sound, miraculous composition, and they were established permanently in their state, not altered, not changed, and not corrupted, preserved from every deficiency and blight. ﴿Then presented in detail﴾ meaning: into kinds of proofs of monotheism, rulings, admonitions, and stories, just as necklaces are detailed with pearls. Or they were made into divisions, surah by surah and verse by verse, or what the servants need was detailed therein, meaning: it was clarified and summarized.

It was said: "Then" (thumma) here indicates a delay in ruling, i.e., in rank, or a delay between the two reports, not a delay in time, because detailing and perfecting are two attributes of one thing, neither of which is separated from the other, so there is no sequence or delay between them. This strained reading is based on the premise that "then" implies sequence, though some have disagreed about its implying that, as related in al-Mughni.

﴿From One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾ meaning: its perfecting and its detailing come from One who is Wise, who founded it on knowledge and wisdom, such that nothing better or more firmly perfected is possible, and who is Acquainted with its details in accordance with what is fitting in the ordering of judgment in its measuring, timing, and arrangement. (Said by al-Qashani.)

Al-Zamakhshari said: In it there is a fine antithesis, because the meaning is that its perfecting was by the Wise, and its detailing, i.e., its explanation and clarification, was by the Acquainted, the Knower of the modes of affairs.

(p-3409) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings.﴾

﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾. Al-Qashani said: That is, he speaks to you through the tongue of state and indication: that you do not associate anyone with Allah in His worship, and single Him out for worship.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Allā" (that… not) is in the accusative as an object of purpose, meaning "lest." Or (an) is explanatory (mufassira), because the detailing of the verses contains the sense of saying, as if it were said: He said, "Do not worship except Allah," or: He commanded you that you not worship except Allah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾ is a statement on the tongue of the Messenger, meaning: indeed I warn you, from the All-Wise, the All-Aware, of the punishment of polytheism and its consequence, and I give you good tidings from Him of the reward of monotheism and its benefit.

The discussion of the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[3] ﴿And that you should seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term and will give every doer of virtue his virtue. But if you turn away, indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day.﴾

﴿And that you should seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ i.e., from polytheism. ﴿Then turn to Him﴾ through obedience. Or the meaning is: then make your repentance sincere and remain steadfast upon it, as in His saying: ﴿Then remain steadfast﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 13].

﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term﴾ i.e., He will prolong your benefit in this world through good and pleasing benefits, of a broad livelihood and successive blessings, until the time of your death, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [an-Nahl: 97].

﴿And will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾ i.e., and He will give every doer of virtue in righteous deeds his reward in this world, and the recompense of his virtue in the Hereafter.

﴿But if you turn away﴾ i.e., turn away from monotheism and from repenting to Him ﴿indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Qashani said: (Great) means: burdensome for you. It is the day of return to Allah, the One Capable of all things, i.e., the day of the manifestation of your incapacity and the incapacity of what you worship, by His manifestation, exalted is He, in the attribute of His capability, so He overcomes you with punishment. For this reason the Exalted said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verses 4–5:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿To Allah is your return, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ [5] ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Hud: 5]

﴿To Allah is your return, and He is over all things Competent.﴾

Then God, exalted is He, made clear their aversion with their bodies as well, following the indication of their turning away with their hearts, by His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests﴾ [Hud: 5], meaning they turn away from the truth and from listening to it with their chests. ﴿To conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal﴾ [Hud: 5], meaning in their hearts. ﴿And what they declare﴾ [Hud: 5], meaning what they utter aloud with their mouths. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [Hud: 5], meaning of what is in the inner depths of the hearts.

A parallel to what is related here about the polytheists of Makkah, regarding their aversion to listening to His speech, exalted is He, is what He said about the people of Noah: ﴿And indeed, whenever I called them, that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and became arrogant with great arrogance﴾ [Nuh: 7]. What we have mentioned is the most apparent meaning the verse can bear, and Allah knows best.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All of it is in a clear register.﴾

﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah﴾ i.e., that by which it lives. The preposition (ʿalā, "upon") was used in consideration of the prior promise concerning it, and to affirm that it reaches them absolutely, by way of a guarantee resembling an obligation. ﴿And He knows its place of settlement﴾ i.e., its dwelling place in this world, or in the loins (al-ṣulb). ﴿And its place of storage﴾ i.e., after death, or in the womb. ﴿All of it﴾ i.e., of the creatures, their provision, their place of settlement and their place of storage, ﴿is in a clear register﴾ i.e., it is inscribed in a register with Him, exalted is He, which makes clear all of that.

Then He, exalted is He, explained the greatness of His power, His shaping and His originating by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 7:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[7] ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. And if you, [O Muhammad], say, "Indeed, you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾

﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ from Sunday to Friday. ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾ meaning: there was nothing beneath it before the creation of the heavens and the earth, and above it, but the water. This is evidence that the Throne and the water were created before the heavens and the earth, as stated in (al-Kashshaf).

The judge (al-Qadi) said: it means there was no barrier between them, not that it was placed upon the surface of the water.

Qatadah said: "In this verse, the Exalted informs us how the beginning of His creation was, before He created the heavens and the earth."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Razin, whose name is Luqayt ibn 'Amir al-'Uqayli, who said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created His creation?' He said: 'He was in 'ama' (a cloud), with nothing beneath it of air, and nothing above it of air, (p-3412) then He created the Throne after that.'" It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan, and he said: Ahmad said: "By 'ama' he means that nothing was with Him."

Al-Bayhaqi said in the book (al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat): "'Ama' is spelled with a long vowel (mamdud), as I have seen it recorded so, and its meaning is a thin cloud, i.e., above a cloud, managing it and exalted over it, as the Exalted said: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16], meaning, He who is above the heaven. His saying '(and nothing above it of air)' means: nothing above the cloud is air. Likewise his saying '(and nothing beneath it of air)' means: nothing beneath the cloud is air."

It has been said that this 'ama' (blindness) is with a short vowel (maqsur), meaning: nothing existent, because it is of what is hidden from creation. So it is as if He said in reply: He was before He created the creation, and there was nothing other than Him. And "ma" in both places is negative, meaning: above the 'ama', which is nothing existent, there is no air, nor beneath it is there air, because if it is non-existent, air cannot be affirmed for it in any way. End, summarized.

Ibn al-Athir said: In the language, 'ama' is a thin cloud; it is said also a thick one, and it is said it is mist. In the hadith there is an omission, meaning: "Where was the Throne of our Lord?" This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾.

Some of them related that it is the short-vowelled 'ama', and said: it is every matter that the intelligent cannot grasp.

Abu 'Ubayd said: "We only interpret this hadith according to the intelligible language of the Arabs as transmitted from them; otherwise we do not know how that 'ama' was!"

Al-Azhari said: "We believe in it and do not specify its manner."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ meaning: most sincere in it. It is connected to (created): that is, He created them for a far-reaching wisdom, which is that He makes them dwellings for His servants, and bestows upon them various kinds of blessings, (p-3413) so that they worship Him alone and compete in the deed that pleases Him. Since testing and examination are for one whose outcome of affairs is hidden from him, it has been said that here it is a figure of speech and metaphor: He likened His treatment of His servants in creating benefits for them, obligating them to thank Him, rewarding them if they are thankful, and punishing them if they disbelieve, to the treatment of an examiner with the examined, in order to know his state and recompense him. So testing was borrowed for Him by way of figurative expression ("that He might test you" in place of "that He might deal with you"). It may also be a metonymy (majaz mursal), because knowledge and examination are mutually implicative; that is: He created that so that it would be known, i.e., so that the connection of His eternal knowledge to that would become manifest.

Al-Qashani said: "He made the ultimate purpose of creating things the manifestation of people's deeds. That is: We created them so that We would know, with detailed knowledge that follows existence and on which reward is based, which of you is best in deed. For the knowledge of Allah is of two kinds: one kind precedes the existence of a thing in the Preserved Tablet, and another kind follows its existence in the manifestations of creation; and the trial, which is examination, is this latter kind." End.

Similar to this verse is His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them without purpose. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾ [Sad: 27], and His saying: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115] ﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 116], and His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you say﴾ that is, to the people of Makkah, ﴿that you will be resurrected﴾ that is, brought back to life ﴿after death, those who disbelieve will surely say: "This"﴾ that is, the claim of resurrection, or the Qur'an which includes mention of it, ﴿is nothing but obvious magic﴾ that is, like it in deception and falsehood.

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[ 8 ] ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted community, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?" Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾

﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted community﴾: i.e., a group of limited periods of time. The punishment is either the punishment of the Hereafter, or the punishment of this world at Badr, or the destruction of the mockers who died before Badr. ﴿They will surely say﴾: i.e., mockingly, ﴿"What is holding it back?"﴾: i.e., from us. ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and there will befall them﴾: i.e., it will surround and descend upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾: i.e., the punishment they used to seek hastily.

A subtle point:

The word (ummah) (community) is used in the Book and the Sunnah with several meanings. It is intended here as a period of time (amad), as in this verse. Another meaning is in His words about Yusuf: ﴿And he remembered after a period (ummah)﴾ [Yusuf: 45]. It also means a leader who is followed, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community (ummah), devoutly obedient to Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 120]. It means religion or creed, as in the verse: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a community (ummah)﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 22]. It means a group, as in the verse: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found upon it a community (ummah) of people watering﴾ [Al-Qasas: 23], and His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent into every community (ummah) a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"﴾ [An-Nahl: 36]. This was reported by Ibn Kathir.

Then, Glorified is He, informed about mankind and the blameworthy qualities within it, except those of His servants who are believers whom Allah has shown mercy, with His, the Exalted's, words:

(p-3415) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then We withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful.﴾

﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ i.e., a blessing, ﴿then We withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing﴾ i.e., he is one who despairs of its return, cutting off his hope in the bounty of Allah, exalted is He, without patience or submission to His decree, ﴿ungrateful﴾, greatly ungrateful for what has passed for him of fluctuating in the blessing of Allah, as if he had never seen any good.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[10] ﴿And if We let him taste ease after hardship had touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾

﴿And if We let him taste ease after hardship had touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me."﴾ That is, the calamities that had distressed me. ﴿Indeed, he is exultant﴾ — that is, insolent and arrogant. ﴿Boastful﴾ — that is, over the people, because of the blessings with which God has let him taste. The joy and the boasting have preoccupied him from giving thanks.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[11] ﴿Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

﴿Except those who are patient﴾ — that is, in adversity, through faith in God and submission to His decree. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ — that is, in ease and in hardship, giving thanks for His bounties, both before and after them. ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾ — that is, for their sins in that hardship. ﴿And a great reward﴾ — that is, for their patience and their righteous deeds.

Admonition:

Al-Qashani, may his secret be sanctified, said: It is fitting for a person, in poverty and wealth, in hardship and ease, in sickness and health, to be trusting in God and reliant upon Him, not veiled from Him by the existence of a blessing, nor by his striving and disposal in earning, nor by his strength and power in seeking, nor by any other means and intermediaries; lest despair arise when those means are lost, and ingratitude, insolence and arrogance arise when they are present, so that he is distanced from God the Exalted by them and forgets Him, and He causes him to forget himself. Rather, he sees giving and withholding as coming from Him alone, not from anything else. If He brings him a mercy of health or a blessing, he thanks Him first by seeing that it is from Him and by witnessing the Benefactor in the form of the blessing; this is done with the heart. Then with the limbs, by employing them in what pleases Him and in obedience to Him, and by fulfilling His rights in them. Then with the tongue, with praise and commendation, being certain that He is able to take them away, guarding them by giving thanks for them, and seeking increase of them, relying on His words: ﴿If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: When the extremities of blessings reach you, do not repel their farthest reaches by scant gratitude. Then, if He takes them from him, let him be patient and not grieve over them, knowing that it is He who took them and no other, for a benefit that returns to him. The Lord the Exalted is like a compassionate parent in raising him, indeed more tender and merciful, for the parent is veiled from what God knows, since he sees only the immediate benefits and their outward aspect, whereas He is the Knower of the unseen and the seen, so He knows what is good for him in this world and the next, being content with His action and hoping that He will return the best of what He took. For one who despairs of His mercy is far from Him; he does not expand to His mercy because of the narrowness of his vessel, veiled from His lordship, not seeing the all-encompassing outpouring of His mercy and its permanence. Then, when He returns them, he does not rejoice in their existence, just as he did not grieve over their loss, nor does he boast of them over people, for that is ignorance and the manifestation of the self. Otherwise he would know that this is not from him or for him. And by what cause would it be proper for him to boast of what is neither his nor from him? Rather, it is for God and from God.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Except those who are patient﴾ are an exception from (man). That is, this kind is despairing and ungrateful, exultant and boastful, in both states, except those who are patient with God, standing firm with Him in the states of adversity and blessing, hardship and ease, as ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: Poverty and wealth are two mounts; I do not care which of them I ride. End.

(p-3417) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you, and your breast would be constricted by it, lest they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?" You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer over all things.﴾

﴿Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you, and your breast would be constricted by it﴾ — that is, by reciting it to them and conveying it to them. ﴿Lest they say﴾ — that is, for fear that they would say, feigning blindness to those proofs whose soundness is hardly hidden from anyone who has even a little insight, and persisting in obstinacy by way of demand: ﴿"Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?"﴾ — that is, "Why was not sent down to him what we have proposed, of treasure and angels," under the claim that the Messenger is one who is followed and must spend on his followers, and that this cannot be accomplished, given his lack of power, except by casting a treasure upon him or by an angel coming with him to attest to his message. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ — that is, it is incumbent upon you only to warn with what has been revealed to you, being unconcerned with the proposals they put forward. ﴿And Allah is Disposer over all things﴾ — that is, He will guard what they say and recompense them for it, so entrust your affair to Him, and convey His revelation with a breast expanded, unconcerned with them.

Subtleties:

The first: al-Qashani said: When they did not accept his speech ﷺ with willingness, and denied his words with corrupt proposals, and met him with obstinacy and mockery, his breast was constricted and he was not at ease in speaking, for willingness draws out speech, and the acceptance of the listener increases the speaker's vigor and makes him expansive in it; and when the speaker finds no receptive place, it does not become easy for him, and it remains a distress to him. So Allah, exalted is He, encouraged him with that and stirred his strength and vigor by His saying: ﴿You are only a warner﴾. Your warning is not free of one of two benefits: either the lifting of the veil so that it takes effect in whomever Allah, exalted is He, has granted success in this, or the establishing of the proof against whomever has not been granted success. Then entrust guidance to Him.

The second: It is not hidden that ﴿perhaps (laʿalla)﴾ is for expectation (tarajji). Although it implies anticipation, it does not follow from the anticipation of a thing that it occurs, nor that its occurrence is preponderant, since there exists what prevents it; and the anticipation of what does not occur is intended here: to incite him to abandon it and to stir up his motive.

It has been said: ﴿laʿalla﴾ here is for remoteness (tabʿid), not expectation, for it is used in that way, as the Arabs say, "Perhaps you will do such-and-such," to one who is not able to do it. The meaning is: "We will not leave it."

It has been said: it is for censuring interrogation (istifham inkari), as in the hadith: "Perhaps we hastened you."

It has been said: it is for the expectation of the disbelievers. Just as it may be for the expectation of the speaker, which is the original usage, since the meanings of performatives (insha'at) subsist in him, it may be for the expectation of the addressee or another who has a connection to its meaning, as here. The meaning is: you have exerted the utmost effort in conveying to them, to the point that they expect from you that you would abandon conveying part of it. Thus in al-ʿInaya.

The third: He turned from the attributive adjective ﴿ḍayyiq (constricted)﴾ to the active participle ﴿ḍaʾiq﴾, to indicate that it is a transient constriction, not fixed; for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most expansive of people in breast. Likewise, every attributive adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), when it is intended to denote occurrence, is transformed into the form of the active participle; they say of sayyid, sa'id; of jawad, jaʾid; of samin, samin (sa'in); and the poet said:

*In a dwelling where the miserly one is fat, while the noble people's traces there are faded.*

The apparent sense of Abu Hayyan's words is that this is analogical (maqis). It has been said that it is for resemblance to ﴿tarik (leaving)﴾. From this it is known that mushakala may be genuine (haqiqa), as in al-ʿInaya.

And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-٣٤١٩)The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful."﴾

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾ means: what is revealed to you. The particle (أم) (am, "or") has two possible readings. It is *munqati'a* (disjunctive), with the implied meaning of (بل والهمزة الإنكارية) (bal, "rather," together with the interrogative hamza of denial), meaning: "Rather, do they say...?" It is also *muttasila* (connective), with the implied meaning: "Are they content with what We have revealed to you, which is the inimitability (al-i'jaz), or do they say that it is not from God?"

﴿Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, and call upon"﴾: the particle (وادعوا) is for seeking help, ﴿whomever you can﴾ means from among humankind and the jinn. The phrase ﴿besides God﴾ is connected to "call upon," meaning: passing beyond God, exalted is He. ﴿if you are truthful﴾ means: in saying that I invented it. For you are Arabs, eloquent like me, especially since you have practiced the methods of verse and prose and of sermons.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of God, and that there is no god but Him. Will you then submit?﴾

﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of God﴾ means: with that which no one else knows, namely a composition (nazm) inimitable for creation, and reports of unseen matters to which they have no path. ﴿And that there is no god but Him﴾ means: and know at that point that there is no god but God, and that His unity is obligatory, and that associating anything with Him is a great wrong. ﴿Will you then submit?﴾ means: will you pledge yourselves to Islam, submitting to the unity of God and to the confirmation of His Messenger after this decisive proof?

[p. 3420] Subtle points (latā'if):

The first: It has been said that they were first challenged with ten surahs, and when they were unable, they were challenged with one surah. Al-Mubarrad held the opposite order. The reasoning is that what occurred first was the challenge with a surah like it in eloquence and in comprising what it comprises of reports of unseen matters, rulings, and their kindred, which are the nine types arranged in the verse of one of them:

Indeed the Qur'an consists of nine kinds of letters, and I shall tell them to you in a line of verse, without tedium:

Lawful, unlawful, decisive, ambiguous, / good tidings, warning, narrative, admonition, parable.

When they were unable to do that, He commanded them to produce ten surahs like it in composition, even if they did not comprise what it comprises. This is supported by its description as ﴿forgeries﴾ (muftarayāt).

It has also been said that the challenge with a surah occurred after establishing the proof for the unity of God and nullifying association, so it was necessary that it be for establishing prophethood by manifesting a miracle, namely the unique surah. The challenge with ten occurred after their obstinacy, mockery, and their demand for signs other than the Qur'an, since they claimed that it was a fabrication. Therefore the situation calls for multiplicity, because it is a matter they regard as fabricated, so producing many like it is not difficult. Thus [it is stated] in (al-'Inayah).

The second: The pronoun in ﴿for you﴾ (lakum) refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the plural is used for honour, as in the words of one who said:

And if I wish, I shall forbid women other than you.

Or it refers to him together with the believers, since they are his followers in the command to take up the challenge. In this there is a subtle admonition that their duty is not to separate from him (upon him be prayers and peace), and to stand with him in opposing those who oppose, as they used to do in jihad. It is also a guidance that this serves to firm up faith and to bring tranquillity in certainty. For this reason His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿so know﴾ etc., are arranged upon it. It is also permissible that the address in the whole be to the polytheists on his behalf (upon him be peace), falling under the command to take up the challenge, and the pronoun in ﴿they do not respond﴾ refers to ﴿whom you can [summon]﴾, meaning: if all those whom you call upon for your affairs do not respond to you with help, then know that this is outside the sphere of human power, and that it is sent down from the Creator of forces and powers. Thus [it is stated] in Abu al-Su'ud.

Then God Most High explained the threat against those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter—namely the disbelievers—by His saying:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, Most High:

[15] ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.﴾

﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived.﴾ That is: We will deliver to them the recompense of their deeds therein, in terms of health and provision.

The discussion of the verse: Allah's saying, the Exalted:

[16] ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein is lost, and what they used to do is null.﴾

﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein is lost﴾ That is: what they did is lost in the Hereafter, meaning there is no reward for it for them. It is also permitted for the adverbial phrase (al-zarf, "therein") to be connected to "did" (ṣana'ū), with the pronoun referring to the worldly life (al-dunya), just as it refers to it in His saying: ﴿We pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾ [Hud: 15]. ﴿And what they used to do is null﴾ That is: their work was in itself null, because they did not work for a sound purpose.

The parallel to this verse is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will enter, blameworthy and rejected﴾ [al-Isra': 18]. ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving while he is a believer – those are the ones whose striving is appreciated﴾ [al-Isra': 19]. ﴿To each – these and those – We extend from the gift of your Lord; and the gift of your Lord is not restricted﴾ [al-Isra': 20]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20].

A subtle point (latifah):

Regarding the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of (bāṭil, "null"), there are two possibilities:

The first: that it is a predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam), with (mā kānū, "what they used to") being a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), and (mā) being either a verbal (maṣdariyyah) or relative (mawṣūlah) particle, and the statement is of the conjoining of sentences (min 'aṭf al-jumal).

The second: that it is a conjunction (ʿaṭf) upon the predicates before it, meaning: "Those – null is what they used to do." And ﴿what they used to do﴾ is the subject (fā'il) of (bāṭil, "null"). This was preferred on the basis of the reading of Zayd ibn 'Alī, may Allah be pleased with them both, who read (wa-baṭala, "and was nullified") in the past tense, conjoined upon (ḥabiṭa, "was lost").

Then the Exalted pointed to the description of the believers, in contrast to "those," with His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 17:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, and before it the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy? Those believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it; indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾

﴿Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord﴾ i.e., a luminous proof of great standing, which indicates the truth of what he has been upon of Islam, and it is the Qur'an. ﴿And a witness from Him recites it﴾ i.e., follows it, ﴿a witness from Him﴾ i.e., from the Qur'an itself, testifying to its being from God, exalted is He, and that is its inimitability. "Clear evidence" (al-bayyinah) has also been interpreted as Islam; he called it "clear evidence" because of the extent of its manifestness, for it is the religion of innate nature (fitrah), before it was defiled by the filth of idolatry. And the "witness" is by the Qur'an, (p-3423) so the pronoun refers to the Lord, exalted is He. ﴿And before it﴾ i.e., before the Qur'an, ﴿the Book of Moses﴾, which is the Torah. That is: the Book of Moses, before it, also follows that evidence, affirming it as well. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a guide﴾ i.e., one to be followed in religion; ﴿and a mercy﴾ i.e., a great blessing upon those to whom it was sent down, guiding them and teaching them the laws. ﴿Those﴾ i.e., those who were upon clear evidence, ﴿believe in it﴾ i.e., in the Qur'an, so for them is Paradise. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions﴾ means the people of Makkah, and whoever joined them of those who banded together against the Messenger of God, may God's blessings be upon him: ﴿the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it﴾ i.e., in doubt concerning the Qur'an or concerning the promised place. ﴿Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe﴾ i.e., in it, either because of the weakness of their insight and the disorder of their thinking, or because of their obstinacy and arrogance.

Subtleties:

The first: "man" (man) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord﴾ is a subject whose predicate has been omitted, because the situation suffices without mentioning it; and this is the secret of the frequent omission of the counterpart of the interrogative hamzah. Its estimate: Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord like those whose deeds were mentioned, and whose destiny and final end were explained — thus said Abu al-Su'ud.

In (Sharh al-Kashshaf) it is that the estimate is: Is one who desires the worldly life, taking it as a relative clause, like "one who has clear evidence from his Lord," with the predicate omitted, indicated by the fa' (then), i.e., they follow them or bring them near. The interrogation is for denial, which implies there is no closeness between them, let alone equality; therefore it became more eloquent than such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner? They are not equal﴾ [al-Sajdah: 18].

The second: "the Book of Moses" has been read in the accusative, as a conjunction upon the pronoun in (yatlūhu), i.e., a witness from among those who were upon clear evidence from their Lord recites the Qur'an, meaning those of the People of the Book who believed, like Abdullah ibn Salam, and their testimony that it is the truth and not fabricated, because of what they find written among them; and (yatlū) is from recitation (tilawah), so the verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 10]. And God knows best.

(p-3424) The third: "al-ahzab" is the plural of hizb, and hizb is a group of people. "Al-ahzab" is applied to those who banded together to wage war against the Messenger of God ﷺ, and likewise every prophet before him; this is a legal (shar'i) usage, and most of the commentators interpreted the verse accordingly, since the surah is Meccan; however, the wording encompasses them and all who resemble them among the rest of the groups.

In Sahih Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, no one from this community hears of me, a Jew or a Christian, then does not believe in me, except that he will enter the Fire." Sa'id said: I used not to hear a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ in its exact form without finding its corroboration in the Qur'an. Then this hadith reached me, so I began to say: Where is its corroboration in the Book of God? Until I found this verse: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾. He said: "The factions" means all the religious communities.

**The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[18] ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ Like his saying to the angels, "they are daughters of Allah," and to the idols, "they are intercessors with Allah." ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾, meaning they will be driven to Him the way slaves are driven before their kings when they have lied against them. ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾, from among the angels, the prophets, and the limbs (al-jawarih): ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.﴾ This is a great terror of what will befall them at that time, because of their wrongdoing in lying against Allah.

It has been said: it is not far-fetched that the verse serves to show that the Qur'an is not a fabrication (muftara), for whoever knows the condition of one who fabricates against Allah, how would he commit it? As passed in Surah Yunus, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the sorcerer does not succeed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 69].

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they are, of the Hereafter, disbelievers.﴾

﴿Those who bar (others) from the way of Allah﴾ i.e., from His upright religion, every person they are able to bar. ﴿And seek to make it crooked﴾ i.e., they seek it to be crooked through disbelief, or they describe it to them as being crooked. ﴿And they are, of the Hereafter, disbelievers.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 20:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Those were not able to escape [Allah] on earth, and they had no protectors other than Allah. Their punishment will be doubled. They were unable to hear, and they used not to see.﴾

﴿Those were not able to escape [Allah] on earth﴾ meaning: they could not escape Him, exalted is He, so as to avoid being punished in this world. ﴿And they had no protectors other than Allah﴾ meaning: they had no one who could shield them from His punishment. ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾ ﴿They were unable to hear﴾ because of their deafness to the truth and their hatred of it. ﴿And they used not to see﴾ because of their blindness to the signs of Allah and their extreme turning away from them, as Allah said: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved and barred [others] from the way of Allah, We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], and so on.

(p-3426) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to fabricate has strayed away from them.﴾

﴿Those are the ones who have lost themselves﴾ i.e., their happiness and their comfort; or by their surrendering themselves to the worship of idols and their abandoning that for which they were created, namely the worship of Him, exalted is He. And this loss of the self is the greatest loss, as it has been said:

Poetry: "If your capital is your life, then guard it against spending it on other than what is obligatory."

﴿And what they used to fabricate has strayed away from them﴾ i.e., the gods and their intercession have vanished from them, and they did not benefit them in the least.

The discussion of the Lord's statement, Exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Without doubt, they are the greatest losers in the Hereafter.﴾

﴿Without doubt﴾ means: truly, or there is no question (lā jaram: "it is certain that"). ﴿That they, in the Hereafter, are the greatest losers.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord — those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord﴾, i.e., they submit humbly to Him alone, ﴿those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally﴾.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿The parable of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Will you not then remember?﴾

﴿The parable of the two groups﴾, i.e., the disbelievers and the believers. ﴿Like the blind and the deaf﴾ is a parable for the disbeliever, ﴿and the seeing and the hearing﴾ is a parable for the believers. ﴿Are they equal in comparison?﴾, i.e., the two groups? ﴿In comparison﴾, i.e., in condition and attribute. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, i.e., by reflecting upon the parables and contemplating them.

(p-3427) Then Exalted is He related to His Prophet (ﷺ) some of the accounts of the messengers by which his heart would be steadied, so that he might be consoled by what he witnesses of the hardship the messengers before him suffered from their peoples, and the severe trials they endured from them, and so that he might inform his people that his mission is like the mission of those who came before him, and that God's way with them is well known, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner, and there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 24], with His saying, glory be to Him:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed I am to you a clear warner."﴾

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾, and the earth had become filled with their polytheism (shirk) and their evils. ﴿Indeed I am to you a clear warner﴾ — that is, "that I am," and it has been read with a kasra (إنّي, inna with kasra). That is: he said, "Indeed I am to you a clear warner, making clear to you the things that necessitate the punishment and the way of deliverance from it."

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.﴾

﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾: The preposition (bāʾ) is implied here for transitivity (taʿdiyah), and (lā) is prohibitive (nāhiyah). That is, We sent him while commanding the prohibition of worshipping other than Allah. ﴿Indeed, I fear for you﴾: that is, if you worship other than Him, ﴿the punishment of a painful day﴾: that is, a painful one, in this world and the Hereafter.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[27] ﴿So the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said, "We see you only as a human being like ourselves, and we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us, immature in judgment. And we see in you no merit over us; rather, we think you are liars."﴾

﴿So the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said﴾, that is, the masters and the great ones. ﴿"We see you only as a human being like ourselves"﴾, meaning: you are not an angel, but a human being, so how is revelation sent down to you above us?

Al-Qashani said: That is, the notables who were occupied with the affairs of this world, capable of them, who were veiled by their intellect and their rational faculty from the truth, ﴿"We see you only as a human being like ourselves"﴾, because they were apparent-minded, standing at the limit of an intellect mixed with illusion, bewildered by desire, which is the intellect of livelihood. They do not see for anyone a station beyond what they have attained by way of intellect, not being aware of the ranks of preparedness and perfections, stage after stage and rank above rank, up to what none knows but God. Thus they did not perceive the station of prophethood and its meaning.

﴿"And we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us"﴾, that is, our poorest and nearest to us in status; for the elevated rank in their view is only by wealth and position, nothing more, as God the Exalted said: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, but of the Hereafter they are heedless﴾ [al-Rum: 7].

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿"immature in judgment"﴾, that is, superficial in judgment; because they are weak of intellect, incapable of earning a living, whereas we are people of thought and reflection. They said this because they were veiled by their deficient intellect from grasping the reality and the moral virtue, since its activity is restricted to earning a livelihood and standing at its limit. As for the followers of Noah, peace be upon him, they were people of lofty aspirations and intellects hovering around holiness, not turning to what others turn to; therefore they lowered their intellects and despised them.

Note:

(bādiya) was read by Abu 'Amr with a hamza, and the rest with a yaʼ.

As for the first, its meaning is the first of opinion, in the sense that it arose without deliberation and reflection, at first glance.

As for the second: it is possible that its origin is what preceded, with the yaʼ replacing the hamza for ease, and it is possible that it is original, from badā yabdū, like ʻalā yaʻlū. The meaning: the apparent opinion rather than its inner reality; had one reflected, its inner reality would have been known, and in meaning it is like the first. In both cases it is in the accusative as an adverb of time. Its governing element is either (we see) or (follows).

Al-Nasir said: These people claimed to argue against Noah by means of those who followed him in two respects:

One of them: that those who followed his opinions are not exemplars or models.

(p-3429) The second: that they, in addition to that, did not deliberate in following him, nor did they profoundly reflect on the soundness of what he brought, but rushed to it without thought or deliberation; and the aim of these people is that no proof be established against them that among them were those who believed him and had faith in him. [End of quotation.]

That is, both aspects demonstrate their ignorance and the shortness of their intellects. As for the first, there is no concealment that it is no disgrace to the truth that the one who follows it is lowly; rather, its followers are the noble, even if they are poor, and those who reject it are the lowest, even if they are rich. Generally, only the weakest of creation follow the truth, just as opposition to it prevails among the great, as God the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We did not send before you a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. When Heraclius, the king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan about the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ, he said among what he said: "Did the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak ones?" He replied: "Rather, their weak ones." Heraclius said: "They are the followers of the messengers."

As for the second: hastening to embrace the truth is among the most exalted virtues, because when the truth becomes clear, there is no room left for opinion or thought, and at that point following it is necessary for every discerning person; only a dullard or a fool hesitates, and nothing is clearer than what the messengers, peace be upon them, call to.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿"And we see in you no merit over us"﴾ is addressed to Noah and his followers, ﴿"over us"﴾, that is, precedence that would qualify you for prophethood and make following you deserving; for merit is confined in their view to wealth and property.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The notables among them were those who had standing and wealth, as you see most of those who profess Islam believing this and building their honoring and humiliating of people upon it. They overlooked that precedence in this world does not bring anyone closer to God; rather it distances him and does not raise him, but lowers him, let alone that it should make him a cause for being chosen for prophethood and qualified for it. Moreover, the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent to encourage seeking the Hereafter and to belittle the affairs of this world and the affairs of those who cling to it. How far their state, peace be upon them, is from being characterized by what distances one from God, and from being honored by what is lowliness in God's sight!

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿"Rather, we think you are liars"﴾, that is, regarding what you claim of reform and of the happiness and salvation that result from it.

The commentary on His words, the Exalted:

[28] ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been obscured to you, shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?"﴾

﴿He said﴾, i.e., Noah. ﴿O my people, tell me﴾, i.e., inform me. ﴿If I am upon clear evidence﴾, i.e., proof ﴿from my Lord and He has given me mercy﴾, i.e., a special, unveiling guidance ﴿from Himself﴾, i.e., beyond the level of reason, from the knowledge of ladunni (divinely bestowed, direct knowledge) and the station of prophethood. ﴿But it has been obscured to you﴾, i.e., because you veil yourselves with the outward from the inward, and with creation from the Truth. ﴿Shall we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?﴾ That is: shall we force you to accept it, and constrain you to be guided by it, while you dislike it and do not choose it? And ﴿there is no compulsion in religion﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 256]. So the interrogation is one of denial, meaning: we are not capable of that. What lies within our power is calling you to God, not forcing you into it. If you wish to receive it, then purify your souls, and abandon your denial. Within his reply, peace be upon him, lies an exhortation to reflect upon it and a rebuke for turning away from it, in a supremely eloquent style.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 29:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿And O my people, I do not ask of you any wealth for it. My reward is only from Allah. And I am not one to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they are going to meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾

﴿And O my people, I do not ask of you for it﴾ meaning, for conveying the tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), ﴿any wealth. My reward is only from Allah﴾. Al-Qashani said: That is, the aim of everything for you is confined to obtaining a livelihood, and I do not seek that from you, so pay attention to my purpose, though you consider yourselves intelligent. (p-3431)

Then, when he made clear that there is no reason to dislike his call, since it does not diminish anything of their worldly possessions, nothing remained except the lowliness of his followers, and that would not be lifted except by driving them away, he said: ﴿And I am not one to drive away those who have believed﴾, meaning, because they are the people of nearness and rank with Allah. Driving them away might prevent them, or others like them, from faith (iman). Only an enemy of Allah who opposes His allies would do such a thing. And even if driving them away were the cause of your faith and they did not apostatize, I would fear their complaint against me for driving them away. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are going to meet their Lord﴾, meaning, they will dispute with their driver before Him. Or the meaning is: they will meet Him and win nearness to Him, so how could I drive them away?

Then he pointed out that their lowliness does not prevent them from faith, since it does not reach them, by His saying: ﴿but I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, meaning, so you fear the lowliness of these people reaching you because of your sharing faith with them, out of your ignorance, since the base person's association is not to be abandoned in every matter. Or, you are ignorant of what qualifies a person for meeting Allah, and you do not know Allah or His meeting, because your minds have departed in this world. Or, you act foolishly and harm the believers, calling them the lowly, or you are ignorant that they are better than you, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them through others, that they might say, "Is it these whom Allah has favored from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53].

Then he pointed out that driving them away entails His punishment, exalted is He, by His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿And, O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then be mindful?﴾

﴿And, O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away?﴾ That is: if driving them away would bring you honour, then I deserve His subjugation by driving them away, and who would protect me from Him? This indicates that driving them away is an injustice that necessarily brings down wrath, definitely. He did not state it explicitly, signalling that it is too evident to need explanation, especially since what hints at their nobility has already preceded, namely their faith in Allah and the Last Day (p-3432). ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ Will you not take heed, so that you refrain from what you are saying?

Admonition:

Some of them said: The fruit of this is the obligation to honour the believer and the prohibition of belittling him, even if he is poor, lacking standing, and engaged in lowly trades. This is because Allah, exalted is He, related Noah's speech and his rebuke of the chiefs when they asked him to drive away those whom they regarded as the base ones. This is akin to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ [al-An'am: 52].

Then he indicated that he, peace be upon him, was a human being like them, who was singled out for revelation and prophethood, so he does not claim what is not his, with his saying:

The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[31] ﴿And I do not say to you, "With me are the treasuries of Allah," nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say, "Indeed, I am an angel," nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon, "Allah will never grant them any good." Allah is most knowing of what is within their souls. Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And I do not say to you, "With me are the treasuries of Allah"﴾ — i.e., His provision and His wealth. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say, "Indeed, I am an angel"﴾ — i.e., I do not claim superiority through prophethood, not through wealth and abundance of property, nor through knowledge of the unseen, nor through being an angel, such that you would deny my superiority for lacking these things. ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon﴾ — i.e., whom you despise, and they are the poor believers. ﴿Allah will never grant them any good﴾ — i.e., in this world and the Hereafter, due to their lowliness before Him, as you say; for the good in my view is what is with Allah, not wealth. ﴿Allah is most knowing of what is within their souls﴾ — i.e., of the good in them, [known to] me and to you; He is more knowing of their worth and standing, and no one knows the extent of their good because of its greatness.

This is what al-Qashani said. Others took this to mean entrusting what is in their souls of faith to the knowledge of Allah, as guidance that it is fitting for everyone not to make a definitive statement except about what he knows with certainty, and to base his affairs on clear evidence, and not to speculate about what he has no clear proof for. ﴿Indeed, I would then be—﴾ i.e., if I said that ﴿among the wrongdoers﴾ — i.e., for diminishing their rights and belittling their standing. For the outward faith manifest from them has raised their status; and when they add to that outward faith the inward faith, as is evident from them, then for them is the reward of the best (ḥusnā). Whoever definitively declares that they will not attain good after they have believed is a wrongdoer. And in this there is an allusion that they (the critics) are wrongdoers in their contempt.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 32:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[32] ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us that with which you threaten us, if you should be of the truthful."﴾

﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation"﴾ That is: you prolonged it, or you brought it in its various forms. ﴿So bring us that with which you threaten us﴾ That is, of the punishment. ﴿If you should be of the truthful.﴾

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[33] ﴿He said: Only Allah will bring it upon you, if He wills, and you cannot escape.﴾

﴿He said: Only Allah will bring it upon you, if He wills﴾ meaning: it is not left to me; rather, Allah, whom you have disbelieved in, is the One who will take charge of it. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾ i.e., by fleeing or by repelling it.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿And my counsel will not benefit you, even if I wished to counsel you, if Allah intends to leave you in error. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

﴿And my counsel will not benefit you, even if I wished to counsel you, if Allah intends to leave you in error﴾ That is: What benefit will my conveying and my counsel, in calling you to monotheism and warning you of the punishment, be to you, if Allah intends to lead you astray so as to destroy you? ﴿He is your Lord﴾ that is, the Master of your affair. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ that is, after death, so that He will recompense you for your deeds. And the words of the Exalted:

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[35] ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit as crime."﴾

﴿Or do they say﴾: that is, the people of Noah. ﴿"He has invented it"﴾: that is, the advice (al-nuṣḥ). It is then part of the continuation of the account of Noah. Or the plural pronoun refers to the disbelievers of Mecca, meaning the fabrication by Muhammad (ﷺ) of the account of Noah. It is introduced parenthetically within the account, as a confirmation of it, an affirmation of its occurrence, and an arousal of the listeners' desire to hear it, since what remains of it is the most important part, namely its outcome. ﴿Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime"﴾: that is, the sin of the earning of my wrongdoing. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit as crime﴾.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 36:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[36] ﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing."﴾

﴿And it was revealed to Noah﴾, meaning: after his great exertion in expending his utmost effort in advising them, while it had not benefited them: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed﴾, meaning: do not grieve ﴿by what they have been doing﴾, meaning: of denial and harm. Their affair has come to its end, and the time for retribution against them has arrived. It has also been said: the meaning is "do not be distressed" for their destruction out of compassion for them, because they are only being destroyed for what they have been doing of obstinacy towards you, so they are not deserving of your compassion nor of Our mercy.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[ 37 ] ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and by Our revelation, and do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾

﴿And construct the ark﴾, that is, for the sake of being delivered from their punishment. ﴿Under Our eyes﴾, that is, under Our protection and care, as though with him from God, Mighty and Majestic, were guardians and watchers who keep it safe with their eyes from the transgression of the disbelievers and from deviation in its construction. ﴿By Our revelation﴾, that is, to you, showing you how to build it, and by Our teaching and inspiration. It was said that there had been no ship before it. ﴿And do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong﴾, that is, do not call upon Me to ward off the punishment from them by your intercession. ﴿Indeed, they are to be drowned﴾, that is, they are decreed to be destroyed by the flood, and this has been determined, so there is no way to avert it, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed there will reach them a punishment that cannot be turned back﴾ [Hud: 76].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 38:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿And he was building the ark, and whenever a group of the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, "If you mock us, then we shall mock you just as you mock."﴾

﴿And he was building the ark﴾: this is a narrated past state (hikayah hal madiyah), used to bring its wondrous form vividly before the mind. It is also said that its implied sense is: "And he began to build the ark." ﴿And whenever a group of the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾, i.e., they scoffed at him, on account of his working on the ship. ﴿He said, "If you mock us"﴾, i.e., regarding the building of the ark, ﴿then we shall mock you﴾, i.e., because of your ignorance, ﴿just as you mock.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[39] ﴿So you will come to know who it is that will receive a punishment that will disgrace him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment.﴾

﴿So you will come to know﴾ ﴿who it is that will receive a punishment that will disgrace him﴾: that is, in this world, so that He makes him an object of mockery. ﴿And upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾: that is, in the Hereafter, in which disgrace will remain with him.

And His words, Exalted is He:

(p-3436)The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven gushed forth, We said: "Load into it two of every kind, a pair, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe." Yet none believed with him except a few.﴾

﴿Until, when Our command came﴾, i.e., with the destruction of his people. "Until" (ḥattā) marks the endpoint of His words "and he was making (the ark)", and what lies between them is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun in it. "They mocked him" [Hud: 38] is the response of "kullamā" (whenever). ﴿And the oven gushed forth﴾, i.e., the surface of the earth, or every spring of water, or the gathering place of a valley's water, or a known spring of water, or the oven (kānūn) in which bread is baked, or the brightening of dawn. These are opinions reported by the lexicographers and the exegetes. Some of them added the possibility that this is a metaphor (kināya) for the intensity of the affair, as one says, "the battle (waṭīs) has become heated" (ḥamiya al-waṭīs), and the waṭīs is the oven. This is among the eloquent and fine expressions of speech. In my view it is the most apparent of the mentioned interpretations, the most delicate, the most original, and the most eloquent, although al-Rāzī attempted to reject it. It is as if it were said: the matter became severe, and the pouring of water and its gushing intensified. This brevity in its terrifying figurative sense has been clarified by other verses, namely: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water﴾ [al-Qamar: 11] ﴿and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar: 12], and so on. Among what supports it is that it encompasses the severity of the affair from both the sky and the earth, which corresponds to these verses. As for other interpretations, they are restricted to the side of the earth alone. It is clear that the matter was more general, and God knows best.

﴿We said: load into it﴾, i.e., into the ship. ﴿Two of every kind﴾, i.e., two categories of beasts, birds, and what crawls upon the surface of the earth. ﴿Two﴾, i.e., a male and a female.

Abu al-Baqa' said: "kull" is read with the genitive (idāfa), and in it there are two aspects:

The first: that the object of "load" is "two," and "min" is a circumstantial element (ḥāl).

The second: that "min" is superfluous (zāʾida), the object is "kull," and "two" is an emphatic restatement (tawkīd). It is also read "min kullin" with tanwīn, so "zawjayn" is the object of "load," "ithnayn" is its emphatic restatement, and "min" is connected to "load" or is a circumstantial element. End of quote.

﴿And your family﴾, i.e., those who are connected to you in your religion and conduct among your relatives. ﴿Except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, i.e., those against whom it became binding to be drowned because of their wrongdoing. ﴿And those who believe﴾, i.e., carry him with you in it. Abu al-Su'ud said: The singular form of "family" is used for the stated exception, and the singular form is preferred in "believed" to preserve the wording of "man" (whoever), to indicate their small number, as His words, mighty and majestic is He, express: ﴿Yet none believed with him except a few.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[41] ﴿And he said, "Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

﴿And he said﴾ — i.e., Noah, peace be upon him, said to those among the believers who were with him: ﴿Embark therein﴾ — i.e., the ship — ﴿in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: It is permissible that this be one sentence and two sentences. The one-sentence reading is that ﴿in the name of Allah﴾ is joined to ﴿embark﴾ as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the waw, meaning: embark therein, invoking Allah by name, or saying "in the name of Allah" at the time of its sailing and at the time of its mooring. This is either because the (noun of) course (majrā) and mooring (mursā) denote the time, or because they are verbal nouns, like "the sailing" (ijrā') and "the sending forth" (irsāl), from which the time, being an implied genitive, has been omitted, as in the expressions "the rising of the star" (khufūq al-najm) and "the arrival of the pilgrim" (maqdim al-ḥājj). It is also permissible that the meaning be the two places of sailing and anchoring. Their accusative case is governed either by what is implied in "in the name of Allah" of the sense of a verb, or by what it contains of the intention of saying.

The two-sentence reading: ﴿in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring﴾ is a nominal clause (jumla ismiyya) that is abrupt (muqtaḍaba), i.e., "in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring." It is related that whenever he wished it to sail he would say, "In the name of Allah," and it sailed; and whenever he wished it to anchor he would say, "In the name of Allah," and it anchored. It is also permissible that the noun "name" be inserted, as in the poet's words:

"Then the name of peace be upon you both"

and the meaning would be: by Allah is its sailing and its anchoring, i.e., by His power and His command. The meaning of our statement "an abrupt sentence" is that Noah, peace be upon him, commanded them to board, then informed them that its course and its mooring are by the mention of Allah's name or by His command and power. It is also possible that it is not abrupt, by being in the position of a circumstantial clause from the pronoun of "the ship," as if it were said: "Embark therein, made to sail and made to anchor, in the name of Allah," in the sense of estimation, like His words: ﴿Enter therein, abiding forever﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. — End.

Remarks:

First: Al-Ikhwan — Ḥamza, al-Kisa'i and Ḥafs — read ﴿majrāhā﴾ with a fatḥa on the mīm, and the rest with a ḍamma. The seven agreed on a ḍamma on the mīm of ﴿mursāhā﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and al-Thaqafi read ﴿marsāhā﴾ with a fatḥa on the mīm as well. It was also read with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the rā' and sīn and a yā' after them, in the form of the active participle, in the genitive position, as two attributes of Allah.

Second: Of the alifs that fall after the rā' and are converted from a yā', which are for the feminine or for the extension, Ḥamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr imāla them; Ḥafs agreed with them in imāla of ﴿majrāhā﴾ here, and no one else did imāla.

Third: Some took from the first reading of ﴿in the name of Allah is its course and its mooring﴾ — I mean the estimate of "saying" — the recommendation of invoking the name (tasmiya) and mentioning Him, exalted is He, at the beginning of the sailing and the mooring. This is reinforced by His words, exalted is He, in Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿So when you are settled, you and those with you, upon the ship, then say: "Praise be to Allah, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 28] ﴿And say: "My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed landing, and You are the best of those who bring to land."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 29] And His words, exalted is He: ﴿And who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them, and say: "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 12–13], to the end of the verse. The Sunna has also come urging this and recommending it.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is a resumptive sentence (jumla mustan'afa), explaining the cause of the deliverance: i.e., had it not been for His forgiveness and mercy you would have drowned and perished like your people. Or it is a reason (ta'līl) for ﴿Embark﴾, because it contains an allusion to salvation; as if it were said: "Embark, so that Allah may deliver you."

And His words, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 42:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[42] ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called out to his son, who was apart, "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾

﴿And it sailed with them﴾ is connected to an omitted element indicated by "board" (ارْكَبُوا), meaning: so board, saying the name of God, while it sails and they are in it. ﴿Through waves like mountains﴾: when the gates of heaven were opened with water and the springs of the earth burst forth, the waters swelled, rose over the sides of the earth, and surged fifteen cubits above the lofty mountains. What rose of the water when it was agitated by its waves was like mountains.

﴿Noah called out to his son, who was apart﴾, that is, separated from his father. ﴿"O my son, board with us"﴾, that is, enter into our religion and accompany us in the ship. ﴿"And do not be with the disbelievers"﴾, that is, in the religion and in isolation, the ones destined to perish.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 43:

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[43] ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." He said, "There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for the One who has mercy." And the wave came between them, so he was among the drowned.﴾

﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, "So I will not drown." ﴿He said, "There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for the One who has mercy."﴾ That is, there is no preventer today from His affliction, which is the Flood, except the Merciful, who is Allah the Exalted. Or: there is no protector except the place of the one on whom He has mercy, and they are the believers, meaning the ship. Or: there is no protector, (p-3440) meaning no one possessing protection except the one whom Allah has mercy upon. Or ﴿except﴾ is disjunctive (munqati'ah), meaning: but the one upon whom He has mercy, he is the one who is protected.

Al-Nasir said: The possible interpretations are four: there is no protector except a merciful one; there is no one protected except a one shown mercy; there is no protector except one shown mercy; and there is no one protected except a merciful one. The first two are exception from the same category (istithna' min al-jins), and the other two are from outside the category. That is, it would be disjunctive. That is: but the one shown mercy is protected, according to the first; but the merciful one protects whomever he wills, according to the second.

Al-Zamakhshari added a fifth, which is: there is no protector except one shown mercy, taking it as from the same category, with the interpretation of omitting the modified noun, its estimate being: there is no protecting place except a place shown mercy. The intent of the negation is an allusion to the mountain's lack of protection, and of the affirmation an allusion to the ship's protection. All of these are permissible, and some of them are closer than others. End of quotation.

﴿And the wave came between them﴾ That is, it became a barrier between Noah and his son, or between his son and the mountain, due to its height above him. ﴿So he was﴾ That is, his son, despite being above the mountain, ﴿among the drowned﴾, that is, those destroyed by drowning.

In this is an indication of the destruction of all the disbelievers in the most emphatic manner, so that this became a matter of fixed occurrence, not requiring explanation. In the use of ﴿kāna﴾ rather than ﴿ṣāra﴾ there is an emphasis on his being among them. (Abu al-Su'ud related this.) Then the Exalted's saying:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 44 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[44] ﴿And it was said: "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold!" And the water subsided, and the matter was decided, and the ark came to rest upon al-Judi. And it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people!"﴾

﴿And it was said: "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold!" And the water subsided, and the matter was decided, and the ark came to rest upon al-Judi. And it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people!"﴾ This informs us that when the people of the earth had drowned, and no dwelling of those who disbelieved in God remained, God, exalted is He, commanded the earth to swallow the water that had gushed out of it and gathered upon it, and commanded the sky to cease the rain. So the water receded, the command of God was carried out by saving whoever was saved and destroying whoever was destroyed.

(p-3441) When the waters began to diminish and retreat into the earth little by little, and the peaks of the mountains appeared, the ship came to rest upon al-Judi, which is a mountain in al-Jazirah near Mosul.

"﴿Bu'dan﴾" (away) is a verbal noun in the accusative, governed by an implied verb, meaning "and they were distanced, a distancing." It is said: "ba'ida ba'da" (he was far away, a distancing) when they intend the utmost distance, in terms of destruction, death, and the like. For this reason it is specific to invocations of evil, like "jad'an" (may he be cut off) and "ta'san" (may he stumble). The "lam" (for) is connected to an implied verb, or it is the lam of explanation, or it is connected to "qila" (it was said), meaning that this saying was said on their account.

The mention of the attribute of wrongdoing serves to indicate that it is the cause of their destruction, and to recall what preceded in His words: ﴿And do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ [Hud: 37].

**Admonition:**

This verse has reached the ultimate in the secrets of inimitability, and it contains the utmost of the rare pearls of excellence. The scholars of rhetoric have been concerned with clarifying choice portions of its subtleties, and among those with the broadest scope in the field of its sciences is the Imam al-Sakkaki. He extended and excelled in his book (al-Miftah) (The Key), and he explained with a gentleness more delicate than the morning breeze. We shall cite it in full, so that minds may be perfumed with the fragrance of its beginning and the musk of its conclusion.

He, may God have mercy on him, said in the discussion of (eloquence [balaghah] and fluency [fasahah]).
