[82] ﴿So when Our command came, We turned it upside down and rained upon it stones of hard clay, layered one upon another, marked from your Lord.﴾

﴿When Our command came﴾, i.e., Our punishment, ﴿We turned it upside down﴾, i.e., those cities were overturned along with their inhabitants, all of them. ﴿And We rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾, i.e., hardened clay, like His words: ﴿stones of clay﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 33]. ﴿Layered﴾, i.e., one part of it was sent down following another, in succession.

Al-Mahayimi said: Some of it was joined to other parts, so that they would be stoned as adulterers are stoned, in a manner fitting their hardness and the rust (rayn) that had penetrated their hearts.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 83:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[83] ﴿Marked from your Lord. And they are not far from the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿Marked from your Lord﴾: distinguished (mu'allamah) with Him. ﴿And they are not﴾, i.e., those stones, ﴿far from the wrongdoers﴾, i.e., those who commit shirk and other transgressions. ﴿Not far﴾: for because of their wrongdoing they deserve them and are subject to them. This contains a severe warning to the people of wrongdoing in general. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the towns, meaning they are near to the wrongdoers of Mecca, who pass by them on their journeys to Syria. The site of those cities has become a body of bitter water that has remained until this day, and it is known as (the Dead Sea), because its waters do not sustain any kind of living creature; and also as (the Sea of Pitch), because it sends up from the depths of its bed to its surface, so it floats upon it; and as (the Lake of Lot), while the land adjoining it is barren and produces nothing.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The masculine form of (far, ba'id) is used either by treating (the stones) as (the stone), or by applying it to a masculine noun understood as (a thing far off), or because it follows the pattern of a verbal noun, like (zafir, the roaring) and (sahil, the neighing). Verbal nouns are used as descriptors equally for masculine and feminine.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The Explanation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[84] ﴿And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day."﴾

﴿And to Madyan⦆ meaning: And We sent to Madyan. It is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with what precedes it. Madyan is a town between the Hijaz and the Levant, near Maʿan, and the name is also applied to its people. They were a people of the Arabs who used to inhabit it.

﴿their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale⦆ meaning: so that you would not defraud people of their goods by falsehood. ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity⦆ meaning: in blessing and wealth in your provision and livelihood, and in well-being and enjoyment in your existence. The meaning is: do not expose yourselves to the loss of that from you by what you do of what you are forbidden from, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day⦆, meaning: a destroying one, or none of them will escape from it.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى:

[ ٨٥ ] ﴿ويا قَوْمِ أوْفُوا المِكْيالَ والمِيزانَ بِالقِسْطِ ولا تَبْخَسُوا النّاسَ أشْياءَهم ولا تَعْثَوْا في الأرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾

﴿ويا قَوْمِ أوْفُوا المِكْيالَ والمِيزانَ بِالقِسْطِ﴾ أي بِالعَدْلِ.

قالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: فَإنْ قُلْتَ: النَّهْيُ عَنِ النُّقْصانِ أمْرٌ بِالإيفاءِ، فَما فائِدَةُ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أوْفُوا﴾ ؟

(p-٣٤٧٦)قُلْتُ: نُهُوا أوَّلًا عَنْ عَيْنِ القُبْحِ الَّذِي كانُوا عَلَيْهِ مِن نَقْصِ المِكْيالِ والمِيزانِ؛ لِأنَّ في التَّصْرِيحِ بِالقَبِيحِ نَعْيًا عَلى المَنهِيِّ، وتَسْيِيرًا لَهُ. ثُمَّ ورَدَ الأمْرُ بِالإيفاءِ، الَّذِي هو حَسَنٌ في العُقُولِ، مُصَرَّحًا بِلَفْظِهِ لِزِيادَةِ تَرْغِيبٍ فِيهِ، وبَعْثٍ عَلَيْهِ، وجِيءَ بِهِ مُقَيَّدًا (بِالقِسْطِ) أي لِيَكُنِ الإيفاءُ عَلى وجْهِ العَدْلِ والتَّسْوِيَةِ، مِن غَيْرِ زِيادَةٍ ولا نُقْصانٍ أمْرًا بِما هو الواجِبُ؛ لِأنَّ ما جاوَزَ العَدْلَ فَضْلٌ، وأمْرٌ مَندُوبٌ إلَيْهِ، وفِيهِ تَوْقِيفٌ عَلى أنَّ المُوَفِّيَ عَلَيْهِ أنْ يَنْوِيَ بِالوَفاءِ القِسْطَ؛ لِأنَّ الإيفاءَ وجْهُ حُسْنِهِ أنَّهُ قِسْطٌ وعَدْلٌ. فَهَذِهِ ثَلاثُ فَوائِدَ. انْتَهى.

﴿ولا تَبْخَسُوا النّاسَ أشْياءَهُمْ﴾ أي لا تَنْقُصُوهم حُقُوقَهم بِطَرِيقٍ مِنَ الطُّرُقِ، كالكَيْلِ والوَزْنِ وغَيْرِهِما، فَهو تَعْمِيمٌ بَعْدَ تَخْصِيصٍ؛ لِأنَّهُ أعَمُّ مِن أنْ يَكُونَ في المِقْدارِ وغَيْرِهِ. والبَخْسُ: الهَضْمُ والنَّقْصُ. ويُقالُ لِلْمَكْسِ: البَخْسُ، قالَ زُهَيْرٌ:

؎أفِي كُلِّ أسْواقِ العِراقِ إتاوَةٌ وفي كُلِّ ما باعَ امْرُؤٌ بَخْسُ دِرْهَمِ

؎ألا تَسْتَحِي مِنّا مُلُوكٌ وتَتَّقِي ∗∗∗ مَحارِمَنا. لا تَتَّقِي الدَّمَ بِالدَّمِ

ورُوِيَ (مَكْسِ دِرْهَمٍ). يُرِيدُ زُهَيْرٌ: أخْذَ الخَراجِ، وما هو اليَوْمَ في الأسْواقِ مِن رُسُومٍ وظُلْمٍ. وكانَ قَوْمُ شُعَيْبٍ يَأْخُذُونَ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُباعُ شَيْئًا، كَما تَفْعَلُ السَّماسِرَةُ، (p-٣٤٧٧)أوْ كانُوا يَمْكُسُونَ النّاسَ، أوْ كانُوا يَنْقُصُونَ مِن أثْمانِ ما يَشْتَرُونَ مِنَ الأشْياءِ، فَنُهُوا عَنْ ذَلِكَ -كَذا في (الكَشّافِ) و(شَرْحِهِ).

قالَ القاشانِيُّ: لَمّا رَأى شُعَيْبٌ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، ضَلالَتَهم بِالشِّرْكِ، واحْتِجابَهم عَنِ الحَقِّ بِالجِبْتِ، وتَهالُكَهم عَلى كَسْبِ الحُطامِ بِأنْواعِ الرَّذائِلِ، وتَمادِيَهُمْ في الحِرْصِ عَلى جَمْعِ المالِ بِأسْوَأِ الخِصالِ -نَهاهم عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وقالَ: إنِّي أراكم بِخَيْرٍ في اسْتِعْدادِكم مِن إمْكانِ حُصُولِ كَمالٍ وقَبُولِ هِدايَةٍ، وإنِّي أخافُ عَلَيْكم إحاطَةَ خَطِيئاتِكم؛ لِاحْتِجابِكم عَنِ الحَقِّ، ووُقُوفِكم مَعَ الغَيْرِ، وصَرْفِ أفْكارِكم بِالكُلِّيَّةِ إلى طَلَبِ المَعاشِ، وإعْراضِكم عَنِ المَعادِ، وقُصُورِ هِمَمِكم عَلى إحْرازِ الفاسِداتِ الفانِياتِ، عَنْ تَحْصِيلِ الباقِياتِ الصّالِحاتِ، فَلازِمُوا التَّوْحِيدَ والعَدالَةَ واعْتَزِلُوا عَنِ الشِّرْكِ والظُّلْمِ، الَّذِي هو جِماعُ الرَّذائِلِ وأُمُّ الغَوائِلِ.

﴿ولا تَعْثَوْا في الأرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ﴾ أي لا تَعْمَلُوا فِيها الفَسادَ. يَعُمُّ أيْضًا تَنْقِيصَ الحُقُوقِ وغَيْرَهُ، كالسَّرِقَةِ والشِّرْكِ، والدُّعاءِ إلَيْهِ، والصَّدِّ عَنِ الإيمانِ ونَحْوِها.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 86:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[86] ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.﴾

﴿What remains with Allah﴾ means His lasting reward, [given] for full measure and weight; or what He has left for you after abstaining from what is forbidden; or the profit He bestows upon you after fulfilling both. ﴿Is better for you﴾ means in your religion and your worldly life. ﴿If you are believers﴾, for indeed the believer is blessed in what he has when he abstains from what is forbidden. Or [it means] ﴿if you are believers﴾ in what I say.

Al-Qashani said: That is, if you believe in the permanence of anything, then what remains for you with Allah of perfections and eternal felicities is better for you than those worldly gains by which you toil and exert yourselves in acquiring and obtaining, and which you then leave behind at death, and nothing remains with you of them except the burden of consequences and the necessary punishment, because of the firmly rooted dispositions in your souls.

﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾ means: a watcher, to keep you from ugly deeds and restrain you from them by force. I am only a messenger and a warner.

(p-3478) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[87] ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we should not do with our wealth what we wish? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning."﴾

﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped"﴾ i.e., of the idols. They answered his command to monotheism with mockery and derision of his prayers, and with the implication that such a thing would not be called for by any sound intellect; rather, what called you to it were whims and whisperings of the same kind as what you persist in. Shu'ayb was much given to prayer, so they gathered together and singled out prayer for mention. It is also read (ṣalātuka) in the singular, as al-Qadi said.

﴿or that we should not do with our wealth what we wish﴾ such as diminishing it and the like. ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning﴾ i.e., the one described among your people as forbearing and rightly guided. They mean that what you command does not match your condition and what you have become known for. Just as the people of Salih, peace be upon him, said: ﴿You were among us a hope before this﴾ [Hud: 62]. Or they said that in mockery of him, and what is meant is that he was the opposite of that. It has been said: this is more likely, because it is more fitting to their mockery before it; and the more precise is the first, because it parallels what Salih was addressed with, and its concluding with the like of what he concluded with, which is His saying, exalted is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[88] ﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and He has provided me from Himself with good provision, [then what?] And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from. I intend only reform, as far as I am able. And my success is not except through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back in repentance."﴾

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾ That is: inform me, if I am upon a certain proof from my Lord, of what He has brought me of action and prophethood. ﴿and He has provided me from Himself with good provision﴾ That is: lawful wealth, earned without diminishing or cheating; or wisdom and prophethood; and perfection and completion, through steadfastness upon monotheism. Is it proper for me to betray the revelation and abandon the prohibition of shirk and injustice, and the reform through purification and adornment? This is an apology for what they denied against him, namely changing what was familiar and forbidding the religion of the fathers. The answer to "tell me" is omitted because what is indicated by the context in such cases, as has passed in the story of Noah and Salih, peace be upon them both. Its particular character here is in his words: ﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from﴾, that is: I do not intend to commit what I forbid you from, so as to take it for myself apart from you. If it were correct, I would have preferred it and would not have turned away from it, let alone forbid it. This was conveyed by al-Qadi.

In (al-Taj): It is said: "He opposed him to the thing": he disobeyed him concerning it, or intended it after he had forbidden him from it, and this is from that.

Al-Qashani said: That is, I do not aim to draw worldly benefits that perish, by committing the injustice that I forbid you from.

﴿I intend only reform, as far as I am able﴾ That is: the reform of your souls through purification and preparation to accept wisdom, as long as I am able and empowered to do it. ﴿And my success is not except through Allah﴾ That is: and my being granted success in reform is only by the help and support of Allah. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾ That is: I depend upon Him. ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾ That is: I return to Him in ease and in hardship.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[89] ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition (shiqaqi) bring upon you the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih. And the people of Lut are not far from you.﴾

﴿And O my people, let not my opposition (shiqaqi)﴾ i.e., let not my enmity (adawati) earn for you ﴿the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih﴾ of drowning, the wind, and the blast (al-sayha). ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you.﴾ For their dwellings are near to you, and you have known what came down upon them of the overturning of the earth and the raining of stones. That is because opposing the messengers necessitates one of these matters.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted: [90] "And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving."

"And ask forgiveness of your Lord" — i.e., from the worship of idols. "Then turn to Him" — i.e., with monotheism (tawhid), or by turning back from defrauding (bakhs) and short-weighting (tatfif). "Indeed, my Lord is Merciful" — i.e., to those who seek forgiveness and repent. "Loving (Wadud)" — i.e., He is intensely loving toward them.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[91] ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and we see you as weak among us. Were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you, and you are not mighty against us."﴾

﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand﴾ i.e., we do not comprehend ﴿much of what you say﴾ such as the Oneness (tawhid) and the prohibition of diminishing (the measure). They mean that they do not accept it, or they said that out of contempt for him, as a man says to one whose speech he does not heed: "I do not know what you are saying!" Or they regarded his speech as raving and confusion, of which little benefits them, and "much" here is meant to signify the whole. Or they said it to flee from obstinacy.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Fiqh (understanding) is knowing the speaker's purpose from his speech; i.e., "we do not understand what you mean." They said this after they had heard from him the proofs of the clear truth in the best and most eloquent manner, and their stratagems were exhausted, so they found no way to dispute with him except turning away from the path of truth and taking the road to misery, as is the habit of one who has been silenced and defeated, who meets clear proofs with abuse, bluster and threats. They made his speech, which contains various kinds of wisdom and admonitions and types of knowledge and insights, into something whose meaning cannot be understood and whose purport cannot be grasped, and they included within that the claim that his words contain what deserves the utmost punishment and retribution. Perhaps this refers to his warning about the consequences for the earlier nations. For this reason they said: ﴿And we see you as weak among us﴾ i.e., you have no strength, so you cannot protect yourself from us if we intend you harm. ﴿Were it not for your clan﴾ i.e., your people, and that they are of our religion ﴿we would have stoned you﴾ i.e., we would have killed you by pelting you with stones, or in the worst manner of killing. ﴿And you are not mighty against us﴾ i.e., you are not honored or esteemed by us, so that we would honor you and protect you from being stoned.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[92] ﴿He said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more powerful over you than Allah? And you have taken Him behind your backs. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do."﴾

﴿He said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more powerful over you than Allah?"﴾ That is: than His command, His revelation and His religion. ﴿And you have taken Him behind your backs﴾ That is: you forgot Him and made Him like a thing cast away behind the back, not regarded at all. The word (ẓihrīyan, "behind the back") is a relative form derived from (ẓahr, "back"), and the vowel-kasra is one of the alterations of relative forms, as they said: (imsī, "of yesterday") with a kasra in the relative form of (ams, "yesterday"), and (dahrī, "of time") with a damma in the relative form of (al-dahr, "time"). ﴿Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do﴾ That is: He is knowing; nothing is hidden from Him, and so He will recompense you.

**The discussion of His words, Exalted is He:**

[93] ﴿And O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. You will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and who is a liar. And watch; indeed I am with you a watcher.﴾

﴿And O my people, act according to your position⦆ That is, according to the extent of your capacity and your ability, or according to your manner and your state in which you are, of your disbelief and your enmity. ﴿Indeed I am acting⦆ That is, according to my position in which I have been, of steadfastness upon Islam and perseverance.

﴿You will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him and who is a liar. And watch; indeed I am with you a watcher⦆ That is, awaiting your destruction. The addition of (with you) shows, on his part, peace be upon him, the complete reliance upon his affair.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: What is the difference between inserting the fa' (fa) and omitting it in ﴿You will come to know⦆? I say: Inserting the fa' is an apparent connection by a particle set for connection, while omitting it is a hidden, estimated connection through the resumptive (isti'naf) which is an answer to an estimated question, as if they had said: "What will happen when we act according to our position, and you act?" So he said: "You will come to know!" So he connected sometimes with the fa', and sometimes with the istinaf, for variety in eloquence, as is the custom of the eloquent Arabs; and the stronger of the two connections, and the more eloquent of them, is the istinaf. End of quotation. That is, to signal that it is something he is asked about and is concerned with, and for this reason it is more eloquent in creating awe.

**Concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[94] ﴿When Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and the Shout seized those who had wronged, so they became prostrate in their homes﴾

﴿When Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾ He mentioned it with *wa* (and), as in the story of 'Ad, since no promise preceded it that would serve as a cause for it, unlike the stories of Salih and Lut. In their case it was mentioned after a promise, namely His saying: ﴿a promise not to be denied﴾ [Hud: 65], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, their appointed time is the morning﴾ [Hud: 81]. Therefore it came with the causal *fa'* (so). This was noted by al-Qadi.

﴿And the Shout seized those who had wronged﴾, i.e., with the punishment, ﴿so they became prostrate in their homes﴾, i.e., dead.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[95] ﴿As if they had never dwelt therein. Ah, away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away.﴾

﴿As if they had never dwelt therein﴾ means: as if they had never settled there. ﴿Ah, away with Madyan, just as Thamud were taken away﴾: He likened them to Thamud, because their punishment was also by the Shout (al-Sayhah, the awful cry), and they were near them in dwelling, peers of theirs in disbelief and in highway robbery, and they were Bedouins like them.

(p-3483) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[96] ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority﴾

﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs﴾, that is, the nine (signs). ﴿And a clear authority﴾, which is the staff. It was the most striking of his miracles, which is why it was singled out. Or it refers to the signs themselves, and the conjunction (ʿaṭf) is for indicating the combination of their being signs and a manifest authority upon his prophethood.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:**

[97] ﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding.﴾

﴿To Pharaoh and his chiefs. But they followed the command of Pharaoh﴾ means: in disbelief in Musa, or in the tyrannical way of Pharaoh.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a declaration that his followers were ignorant, in that they went along with his command, and it is a manifest error that is not hidden from anyone who has even a little measure of intellect. This is because he claimed divinity while being a human like them, and he openly practised oppression, injustice and evil, which only comes from a rebellious devil. Yet they followed him, submitted to his claim, and hastened to obey him.

﴿And the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding﴾ means: not guiding, or not possessing rectitude; rather, it was misguidance and error.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 98:

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[98] ﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are led.﴾

﴿He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection﴾ meaning: he will go before them to the Fire, just as he used to lead them in this world to misguidance. ﴿And lead them into the Fire﴾ meaning: he will bring them to it. The use of the past tense (fa-awradahum, "and led them") is to indicate that it is certain to occur and to affirm it definitively. He likened Pharaoh to the forerunner (al-farit) who goes ahead of those coming to water (al-warida), and his followers to those coming to water, and the Fire to the water which they come to.

Then it was said: ﴿And wretched is the watering-place to which they are led﴾ meaning: wretched is the watering-place that the Fire is for them, because the watering-place (al-wird), which is the portion of water, is only sought to quench thirst and cool the liver (kabid), whereas the Fire is the opposite of that.

(p-3484) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[99] ﴿And they were followed in this (world) by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection. Wretched is the gift that is given.﴾

﴿And they were followed in this﴾, i.e., in this world, ﴿by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., they are cursed in this world and in the Hereafter. The curse follows them wherever they are. Thus, "يَوْمَ" (yawm, "day") is grammatically coordinated with the position (maḥall) of "فِي" (fī, "in") in "هَذِهِ"; it is not the start of a new sentence.

﴿Wretched is the gift that is given﴾, i.e., wretched is the gift bestowed, and it is the curse in both abodes.

The discussion of the words of His Most High:

[100] ﴿That is among the reports of the towns which We relate to you; some of them are still standing, and some are reaped down.﴾

﴿That﴾ is a reference to what has been related of the reports of the nations. ﴿Among the reports of the towns﴾, i.e., the destroyed ones. ﴿We relate it to you﴾, i.e., by revelation. ﴿Some of them are standing﴾, i.e., remaining, still visible to the eye, though their people have perished. ﴿And some are reaped down﴾, i.e., and among them are those whose traces have been effaced, like a field of crops that has been harvested.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[101] ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came, and they added nothing to them but ruin.﴾

﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by destroying them, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾, that is, by exposing themselves to what necessitated for them polytheism (shirk), the worship of idols, and wrongdoing. ﴿So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came, and they added nothing to them but ruin﴾, that is, destruction and loss (takhsir).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 102:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[102] ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾

﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ In it is an indication of their wrongdoing, and an announcement of His, may He be exalted, sunnah (established way) in seizing wrongdoers, which does not change, and a warning to every wrongdoer who has wronged himself or others of the evil consequence.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[103] ﴿Surely in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day that will be witnessed.﴾

﴿Surely in that﴾, i.e., in what has been related in this surah, or in the seizing of the wrongdoers, ﴿is a sign﴾, i.e., a lesson (ʿibrah), ﴿for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter﴾, so that he takes heed from it, away from what necessitates it. ﴿That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day that will be witnessed﴾, i.e., it will be witnessed by the first and the last, and by the people of the heavens and the earth.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[104] ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term.﴾

﴿And We do not delay it﴾ — that is, the Day; ﴿except for a limited term﴾ — that is, for a bounded duration.

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[105] ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them will be the wretched and the blessed.﴾

﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission﴾ — that is, by the permission of Allah, exalted is He, as in His saying: ﴿None will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct﴾ [al-Naba relates: 38]. ﴿Among them will be the wretched and the blessed.﴾

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[106] ﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; for them therein will be groaning (zafir) and wailing (shahiq).﴾

﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; for them therein will be groaning (zafir) and wailing (shahiq).﴾ Al-zafir is the expelling of breath accompanied by a prolonged sound, and al-shahiq is its drawing back in. Both are used as metaphors for distress and anguish, because breath commonly rises heavily along with them. Or [the verse] likens their shrieking to the braying of donkeys.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[107] ﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends.﴾ [108] ﴿As for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a gift unbroken.﴾ [Hud: 108]

﴿Abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends.﴾ ﴿As for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a gift unbroken.﴾ [Hud: 108] That is: not cut off, but extending without end.

Regarding the specification by "the heavens and the earth" there are two aspects. The first: that it is an expression for perpetuity and the negation of cessation, like the Arabs' saying: "as long as Thabir stands" (ma aqama Thabir), "as long as a star shines" (ma laha kawkab), "as long as the sea surges" (ma tama al-bahr), and the like. Their abiding in both abodes is not made dependent on the continuance of these heavens and earth, for the texts indicate the perpetuity of their abode and the cessation of the continuance of those two.

The second: that what is meant is the heavens and earth of the Hereafter, since its people must have something that shades them and something that sustains them. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿On the day the earth will be replaced by other than the earth, and the heavens [as well]﴾ [Ibrahim: 48], and His saying: ﴿And He has given us the earth, to take up residence in the Garden wherever we will﴾ [al-Zumar: 74].

If you say: what is the meaning of the exception by the will, when the eternal abiding of the people of both abodes therein has been established without exception? The answer is what we mentioned earlier regarding His saying: ﴿Say: I possess not for myself any benefit or harm except as Allah wills﴾ [al-A'raf: 188]. That is, the exception by will has been used in the style of the Qur'an to indicate firmness and continuity.

The point of the exception is to show that these established, permanent matters are so only by the will of Allah, the Exalted, by their own nature; had He willed to change them, He would have done so.

Ibn Kathir alluded to this with his words: meaning that their continuance is not a matter necessary in itself, but is entrusted to His, the Exalted's, will.

And Ibn 'Atiyya with his words: this is by way of the exception which the Lawgiver urged to be used in every speech, like His saying: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills﴾ [al-Fath: 27]; it does not need to be described as either connected or disconnected.

There are many interpretations of the scholars here, and what we have mentioned is the most correct and the most original of them.

When the Exalted related the stories of the idol-worshippers and mentioned the vengeance He brought upon them and the punishment He prepared for them, He said:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[109] ﴿So do not be in doubt about what these worship. They worship only as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share undiminished.﴾

﴿So do not be in doubt about what these worship﴾ means: do not be in doubt about their worship, [about] its being misguidance that leads to the like of what befell those before them. In this there is consolation for him (ﷺ), a promise of retribution, and a warning to them. ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before﴾ means: they are alike in associating partners [with God], and what befell their fathers has reached you, so the like of it will surely befall them. This is a resumptive clause giving the reason for the prohibition against doubt. ﴿And indeed, We will give them their share﴾ means: of the punishment, just as We paid their fathers in full, ﴿undiminished﴾.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:**

[110] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it was disputed concerning it. Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them. And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, i.e., the Torah. ﴿But it was disputed concerning it﴾, i.e., some people believed in it and others disbelieved in it, just as these people have disputed about the Qur'an. ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, meaning what was indicated in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33]. ﴿It would have been decided between them﴾, i.e., by their annihilation. ﴿And indeed they﴾, i.e., these people, namely the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿are in doubt concerning it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿disquieting﴾, i.e., causing people to fall into suspicion.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 111:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[111] ﴿And indeed, to each your Lord will surely pay in full their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.﴾

﴿And indeed, to each your Lord will surely pay in full their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.﴾ That is, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for it. The tanwin in (kullan) is a substitute for the omitted noun, meaning: "And indeed, all of those who differ concerning it."

Note:

In this verse there are readings. (In) and (lamma) are read both lightened and doubled, and (in) lightened with (lamma) doubled, and the reverse. These four readings are all mutawatir (transmitted by a multitude of narrators at every stage).

As for the first: it involves the operative (in) (lightened), which is a well-established dialect of the Arabs. The lam in (lima) is the lam of the beginning (lam al-ibtida', the emphatic lam), entering on the predicate of (in). The (ma) is either a relative pronoun meaning (alladhina), referring to those who have intellect, and the lam in (layuwaffiyannahum) is the answer to an implied oath, meaning: "And indeed all of them, for those who [...], by God, He will surely pay them in full." Or it is an indefinite qualified noun, and the oath clause with its answer is the qualifier of (ma), meaning: "And indeed all of them are a creation, or a group, and by God He will surely pay them in full." It has been said: the first lam is a preparatory lam for the oath, and when the two lams came together and agreed in form, they were separated by (ma), which is then extra, for the sake of the correction of the pronunciation. It has been said: the lam mentioned is the one that distinguishes the lightened (in) from the negative (in). It has been said: it is the answer to the oath, repeated for emphasis.

As for the second reading, namely the doubling of both: (in) remains as it is, and what follows it is in the accusative as its subject, and (lamma) means (illa) (except), or is a jussive particle meaning (lam) (not), with its jussive object omitted, meaning: "not yet have they been given respite," or "not yet have they been paid their deeds until now, and they will be paid them."

As for the third reading, namely the lightening of (in) and the doubling of (lamma): (in) is lightened and operative as shown above, and (lamma) means (illa) or is also jussive, or (in) is negating like (ma), and (lamma) means (illa), and (kullan) is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, meaning: "And I do not see all of them except..."

As for the fourth reading, namely the doubling of (in) and the lightening of (lamma): it is clear, since (in) is the doubled one and it operates in its normal manner.

The discussion of the (lam) and (ma) is like what was mentioned first of the four aspects concerning the (lam) and the three concerning the (ma).

There are other readings, so let them be consulted in (al-Samin) and elsewhere.

And His saying, exalted is He:

**The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[112] ﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded, and those who turn [in repentance] with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾: that is, in the Qur'an. The (الكاف) here is for comparison, or it carries the meaning of (على). ﴿And those who turn [in repentance] with you﴾: that is, from polytheism, and they are the believers. ﴿And do not transgress﴾: that is, do not exceed the limits of God. ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾: that is, He will recompense you for it.

Ibn Kathir said: He, Exalted is He, commands His Messenger and the believers to persevere and remain constant in steadfastness, and that is among the greatest aids to victory. He forbids tyranny, which is oppression (al-baghy), for it is a cause of downfall, even if it is directed against a polytheist.

[p. 3490] On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[113] ﴿Do not incline toward those who wronged, lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah; then you would not be helped.﴾

﴿Do not incline toward those who wronged﴾, i.e., who wronged themselves through polytheism and sins. That is: do not settle down with them, and do not be at ease with them, because inclining toward them leads to approval of their polytheism, strengthening them, and weakening the side of truth. ﴿Lest the Fire touch you, and you have no protectors other than Allah﴾, i.e., no helpers who could ward off His punishment from you through your inclining toward them. ﴿Then you would not be helped﴾, i.e., you would not be able to prevent what is intended for you. The purpose is to keep the believers away from showing affection to the polytheists who oppose Allah and His Messenger, and from placing trust in them, for they are the greatest obstacle in turning people away from the way of Allah, since such conduct contradicts faith.

It has been said: this verse is among the most forceful forms of prohibition against wrongdoing and warning against it, for if this severe threat applies to one who inclines toward its people, how much more to one who immerses himself in their filth?

Note:

Some Yemeni exegetes said: the verse clearly states that inclining toward wrongdoers is forbidden and a major sin, because Allah, exalted is He, threatened it with the Fire. But what is the inclining that He intended? We say: there are several views on this.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Asamm that the meaning is: do not lean toward the wrongdoers in any matter of your religion.

It was also said: that you approve of their deeds. This is related from Abu al-ʿAliyah.

It was also said: that you join the polytheists. This is related from Qatadah.

It was also said: that you flatter the wrongdoers. This is related from al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

It was also said: entering with them into their wrongdoing, showing approval of their actions, and showing loyalty to them. As for entering upon them to repel their evil, it is permissible, because Allah commanded gentleness in dealing with the disbelievers, and wrongdoers are more deserving of it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the prohibition covers yielding to their desires, depending on them, keeping company with them, sitting with them, visiting them, flattering them, approving of their deeds, imitating them, adopting their attire, casting one's eyes on their finery [p. 3491], and mentioning them in a way that glorifies them. Reflect on His saying, ﴿do not incline﴾, for inclining is a slight tilt. And His saying, ﴿toward those who wronged﴾, meaning toward those among whom wrongdoing was found, and He did not say "toward the wrongdoers."

It is related that al-Muwaffaq prayed behind an imam, who recited this verse, and he fainted. When he came to, he was asked about it, and he said: "This is about one who inclines toward those who wronged; so what of the wrongdoer himself?" (End of quotation.)

Al-Yamani said: scholars have been lenient in this matter and also strict, and circumstances differ, and actions depend on intentions, and detailed distinction is preferable. If the association is to repel an evil, or to seek help against it, or in hope of their abandoning wrongdoing, or to ward off their harms, then there is no blame in it, and it may even be obligatory. But if it is for the sake of their companionship and approval of them, then it is not permitted. (End of quotation.)

I say: all of this is based on the general application of the verse. As for whether it refers to the polytheists of Makkah, relying on the verse's context and flow, then what is meant by it is what we mentioned first, and Allah knows best.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[114] ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾

﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ i.e., at morning and evening. ﴿And in some hours of the night﴾ i.e., and during some of its hours, namely those close to the end of the night, from (azlafahu), meaning "to bring near," and izdalafa ilayhi, "to draw near to it." The prayer of the morning (al-ghadwah) is the Fajr, and the prayer of the evening (al-'ashiyyah) is the Zuhr and the 'Asr, because what comes after midday is 'ashiyy (evening). The prayer of the zulaf is the Maghrib and the 'Isha', as stated in al-Kashshaf.

This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Establish prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn﴾ [al-Isra': 78], in that the two combine the five prayers in a manner that is extremely eloquent in its concision. The accusative of (tarafay al-nahar) is as an adverbial of time, since it is annexed to it. As for (zulafan), the common readers recite it with a damma then a fatha, the plural of zulfah, like zulmah and zulam. It was also read with damma on both letters, either as the plural of zulfah with its middle letter vowelled with damma to match its first letter, or as a singular noun like 'unuq, or as the plural of zalif in the sense of zulfah, like raghif and rughuf.

It was also read with a sukun on the lam, either lightened, in which case the preceding readings apply, or with the sukun in its original form, like busrah and busr, without assimilation.

It was read as (zulfa) like hublan, in the sense of "near," or by replacing the alif for the tanwin, treating pausal form as continuous recitation. Its accusative is either adverbial, being conjoined to (tarafay al-nahar) since what is meant is hours, or conjoined to (al-salah), in which case it is an object.

According to Tha'lab, al-zulfah is the first hours of the night. Al-Akhfash said: it is any hours of the night, and its original meaning is nearness; it is said izdalaf, meaning "drew near." (min al-layl) is an attribute of zulafan, as stated in al-'Inayah.

﴿Indeed, good deeds﴾ i.e., those of which the prayers you have been commanded are part, indeed their foundation, ﴿erase bad deeds﴾ i.e., those of which humans are rarely free, meaning they expiate them. ﴿That﴾ i.e., establishing the prayers at the mentioned times, ﴿is a reminder for those who remember﴾ i.e., a reminder of Him, exalted is He, and a bringing of the heart into His presence, and a purifying from the turbidity of heedlessness and forgetfulness, out of awe of Him.

It has been narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, I embraced a woman at the far end of the city, and I touched her with what is less than intercourse, and here I am, so decide my case as you wish! 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: Allah would have concealed you had you concealed yourself. He said: The Prophet ﷺ did not answer him with anything. The man stood and went away, so the Prophet ﷺ sent a man after him and called him and recited to him this verse: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night; indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds﴾, etc."

A man from the people said: O Messenger of Allah, is this specific to him? He said: "Rather, it is for all people." Al-Bukhari and others recorded it.

In another narration from Abu Umamah: the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Did you complete the ablution and pray with us?" He said: Yes. He said: "Then you are free of your sin as on the day your mother bore you, so do not return," and he recited the verse.

In another narration: "Then the verse was revealed." The meaning of revelation here is its encompassing, by its earlier revelation, what occurred, since it was the cause of the revelation, as we have explained more than once.

In the Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Tell me, if there were a river at the door of one of you in which he bathed every day five times, would any of its filth remain?" They said: No. He said: "That is the likeness of the five prayers, by which Allah erases sins." Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Jabir, and something similar is narrated from 'Uthman and Salman.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Mu'adh that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Follow a bad deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and treat people with good character."

He also narrated from Abu Dharr, raised to the Prophet ﷺ: "When you do a bad deed, follow it with a good deed and it will erase it." I said: O Messenger of Allah, is the saying "There is no god but Allah" among the good deeds? He said: "It is the best of good deeds." That is, the good deeds are like the prayer, dhikr, charity, seeking forgiveness, and similar acts of righteousness.

A subtle point:

Al-Qashani, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed to the secret of the five prayers at their times with what deserves reflection, and he said:

Since the five senses are distractions that occupy the heart with what arrives at it in bodily forms, drawing it away from the divine presence, veiling it from light and presence, by turning away from the side of holiness and facing the source of impurity, replacing its loneliness with intimacy and its turbidity with clarity, five prayers were prescribed, in which the servant empties himself for presence and closes the doors of the senses, so that no distracting thing arrives at the heart to occupy it. By opening the door of the heart to Allah, exalted is He, through turning and intention, light's supply arrives; and it gathers its concern from dispersal, and finds intimacy with its Lord from loneliness, along with the unity of direction and the attainment of collectedness. Thus those prayers become five open doors for the heart toward the presence of the Lord, through which light enters opposite those five open doors to the side of delusion, and a dwelling for the deceiving eye, through which darkness enters; so that the light arriving removes the traces of its darkness and sweeps away the dust of its turbidities. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds﴾.

It has come in a hadith: "Prayer to prayer is an expiation for what is between them, so long as the major sins are avoided." He commanded establishing it at the two ends of the day, so that its ruling may extend, by the continuance of collectedness and the dominance of the luminous state, at its beginning to the rest of the times, so that perhaps one will be among those who are constant in their prayer, due to the continuance of that presence and the remaining of that light, and at its end it sweeps and removes what occurred in the rest of the times of dispersal and turbidity. And since the natural powers that govern the matter of nourishment have their dominion at night, and they draw the soul to managing the body through sleep, away from its spiritual world, and restrain it from its own proper affair, which is contemplating the world of holiness, by occupying it with using the instruments of nourishment for the building of the body, so that they strip it of subtlety and cloud it with haze, there was a need to refine and purify it by wakefulness, and to illuminate it by prayer. Thus He said: ﴿And in some hours of the night﴾. End. And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[115] ﴿And be patient, for indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.﴾

﴿Be patient﴾ means: upon the hardships of what you have been commanded regarding conveying the message, or upon what they say, or upon the prayer, like His saying: ﴿And be steadfast in it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. There is no obstacle to its including all of these.

﴿For indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾ means: in their deeds, so He pays them their rewards in full, without any diminution.

Abu al-Su'ud said: He expressed this by negating loss, to show the perfection of His exaltedness above that, by depicting it in the form of something whose occurrence from Him, glorified is He, is impossible, and by presenting the granting of reward in the manner of obligatory matters, along with an indication that patience upon what has been mentioned is of the category of doing good. End of quote.

Al-Shihab, in (al-'Inayah), pointed out here a subtle point of Qur'anic eloquence: that commands to acts of goodness were addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the singular, although they are general in meaning, whereas the prohibitions were addressed to the community in the plural.

And His exalted saying:

(p-٣٤٩٦) On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[116] ﴿Why were there not among the generations before you people of virtue who would forbid corruption in the earth, except for a few of those whom We saved from among them? But those who did wrong pursued the luxuries they had been given, and they were criminals.﴾

﴿Why were there not﴾ means: why was there not found ﴿among the generations before you people of virtue who would forbid corruption in the earth﴾, that is, by committing evil deeds and reprehensible acts. For if there had been among them those who forbade, the rest would not have been seized. ﴿Except for a few of those whom We saved from among them﴾ is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes). That is: but a few of those whom We saved from the generations did forbid corruption, while the rest abandoned forbidding.

A subtle point:

(al-baqiyya) may mean "the remaining one" (al-baqiya), with the feminine ending referring to the quality or the portion. Or it may mean "a remnant of judgment and reason." Or it may mean "excellence," with the ta' marking its transfer into a noun, as in al-dhabiha (the slaughtered animal). The word baqiyya was applied to excellence as a metaphor (isti'ara) drawn from the remnant that a person sets aside for himself and saves from what he spends, since he chooses the best of it for himself. Hence it is said: "In corners lie hidden things, and among men, remnants," and "So-and-so is of the remnant of the people," meaning of their best. It is also permitted that al-baqiyya be a verbal noun (masdar) meaning al-baqwa (preservation), like al-taqiyya meaning al-taqwa (piety). Then the meaning would be: why was there not among them people of self-preservation, who guarded themselves from His wrath and punishment?

﴿And those who did wrong pursued the luxuries they had been given﴾ means: what they had come to enjoy of desires, until the punishment overtook them suddenly. Pursuing it is a metonymy (kinaya) for concern with it and neglect of anything else, as is the habit of one who follows something.

﴿Those who did wrong﴾ is more general than those who directly committed corruption themselves and those who abandoned forbidding it. al-Zamakhshari restricted it to the second group, because they were the intended target of the censure that came before it, where he said: "By ﴿those who did wrong﴾ He meant those who abandoned forbidding reprehensible acts, that is, they did not concern themselves with what is a great pillar of the religion, namely enjoining good and forbidding evil. They set their aspirations on desires, pursued what they knew to be luxury and affluence, out of love of leadership and wealth and the pursuit of the means of a pleasant life, and they rejected what lay beyond that and cast it behind their backs."

(p-٣٤٩٧) ﴿And they were criminals﴾ means: by their aforementioned pursuit, or disbelievers. al-Qadi said: "It seems he intended to explain what was the cause of the destruction of the earlier nations, namely the spread of wrongdoing among them, their following of desire, and their abandonment of forbidding reprehensible acts together with disbelief. This was alluded to by His words, exalted is He:

The discussion of the Almighty's words:

[117] ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers.﴾

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers.﴾ That is, by their enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. As for (unjustly, bi-zulm), the "bi" in it may be for accompaniment (al-mulabasah), in which case it is a circumstantial clause (hal) of the subject: that is, it is impossible in wisdom that He should destroy the towns while being unjust to them. Its indefiniteness (in the Arabic, zulm is indefinite) is for magnification, and to signal that destroying reformers is a great injustice. Or the "bi" may be causal (al-sababiyyah). Injustice here means shirk (associating partners with God): that is, He does not destroy the towns on account of their people's shirk while they are reformers, who deal justly among themselves and do not add to their shirk another corruption. This is due to the abundance of His mercy and His forbearance regarding His own rights. Hence it has been said: "Dominion persists with shirk, but does not persist with injustice." And this, though correct, does not fit the context of the messengers' call to monotheism and the erasure of shirk first, then to uprightness in dealings second; the context requires that (injustice) here be understood as more general than shirk, encompassing categories of sins. And the reform is understood as their reforming it, desisting from it, with some of them being engaged in forbidding it and some of them inclined toward admonition, not persisting in what they are upon of shirk and the like. Thus Abu al-Su'ud indicated.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 118:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[118] ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ﴾

﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community﴾, i.e., united upon the truth, faith, and righteousness, but He did not will that. ﴿But they will not cease to differ﴾, i.e., concerning the truth: among them is the one who believes in it, and among them is the one who disbelieves in it.

(p-3498) The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[119] ﴿Except those on whom your Lord has mercy. For that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾

﴿Except those on whom your Lord has mercy﴾: that is, but some people whom He has shown mercy by guiding them to monotheism (tawhid) and enabling them to attain perfection. They agreed in their creed and purpose, and conformed in their conduct and way. Their direction (qiblah) is the Truth, and their religion is monotheism and love.

As for His, the Exalted's, words, ﴿For that He created them﴾, there are several opinions regarding what the pronoun refers to. The most apparent is that it refers to the difference indicated by "(mukhtalifin)" (differing), so the pronoun then refers to mankind. That is, He created them for the fruit of the difference, namely that one group is in Paradise and another group is in the blaze. The lam here is the lam of consequence and outcome (lam al-'aqibah wa al-sayrurah), because the wisdom behind their creation is not this, due to His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], and because if He had created them for this, He would not have punished them for it. Alternatively, the demonstrative refers to this and to the mercy understood from "(rahima)" (had mercy), by interpreting it as "(an and the verb)" (that-clause with a verb), or by considering it to mean good. The demonstrative would then refer to two things, as in His words: ﴿neither old nor young, but between that﴾ [al-Baqarah: 68]. The meaning is: He created them for the difference of all of them and the mercy of some of them. This is attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father. If the pronoun refers to "(min)" (some), then the demonstrative refers to mercy by the earlier interpretation. This is what is stated in al-'Inayah.

Al-Qashani indicated that the lam remains in its meaning, which is causation by another aspect. He said: "And He created them for the difference, so that each of them would be prepared for a matter and a work, and would choose by his nature a task and a craft. Thus the order of the world is established, and the affairs of livelihood are sound. They are carriers of Allah's command: He loaded upon them the loads of causes and provisions and what people live by, and He arranged through them the foundation of worldly life. Just as the merciful group are manifestations of His perfection, Allah manifested through them His attributes and actions, and made them the repository of His wisdom, knowledge, and secrets."

(p-3499) As for His, the Exalted's, words, ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾: that is, it has been decreed, confirmed, and established. It is this: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ By "jinn and mankind" is meant their disobedient ones, and the definiteness is for specific reference (al-'ahd). The indication is rational, since it is known from the law that punishment is specific to them and that the threat applies only to them. There is no need to estimate an omitted noun (mudaf), as has been said. With "(all together)" then being apparent, even if it is not taken as referring to a specific group and is kept in its general sense, the benefit of emphasis is to clarify that the filling of Hell is from both categories, not from only one of them. Those among them who enter it are left unspecified, entrusted to His, the Exalted's, knowledge. Thus the objection raised against its apparent meaning, namely that it requires the entry of all of both groups into Hell, is dismissed, and its falsity is known by necessity. As for the first interpretation, this is clear. As for the second, the meaning of the word "(all together)" is the inclusion of the categories, and that does not require the entry of every individual, just as when you say: "I filled the sack with all kinds of food," this does not require that the sack contain every individual item of food, but only that it contain some of each kind. Likewise, your saying: "The assembly was filled with all kinds of people" does not require that every individual person be in the assembly, but that there be one of each kind. This is evident. In light of this, the benefit of the word "(all together)" becomes clear, for it refutes the Jews and others who claimed that they will not enter the Fire. This is what is stated in al-'Inayah.

When He, the Exalted, mentioned in what preceded the reports of past nations and bygone generations, and what happened to them with their prophets, He here pointed to the secret and wisdom of that, through His words:

The discussion of the Lord's words:

[120] ﴿And We relate to you the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart. And there has come to you in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.﴾

﴿And We relate to you the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart﴾ means: We strengthen your heart by it, so that you may endure the harm of your people, follow the example of the messengers before you, and know that the final outcome is yours, just as it was theirs. The word ﴿كُلًّا﴾ (kullan, "all of them") is the object of ﴿نَقُصُّ﴾ (naqussu, "We relate"), and ﴿مِن أنْباءِ﴾ (min anba'i, "from the news of") explains it. The phrase ﴿ما نُثَبِّتُ﴾ (ma nuthabbitu, "by which We strengthen") is either a substitute (badal) for ﴿كُلًّا﴾ or the predicate of an omitted subject.

(p-3500) ﴿And there has come to you in this﴾, i.e., in this surah, or in the related news, ﴿the truth﴾, i.e., the true, established account. ﴿And an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾, i.e., a lesson for them by which they guard themselves against what destroyed the nations, and a reminder of what they must hold themselves accountable to, making it their path and their way of life.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[121] ﴿And say to those who do not believe: "Act according to your position; indeed we are acting."﴾

﴿And say to those who do not believe﴾ — that is, in this truth, and who do not heed admonition or take heed. ﴿Act according to your position﴾ — that is, according to your state of following desires. ﴿Indeed we are acting﴾ — that is, we are acting according to our state of following what has come to us, heeding admonition and taking heed of it.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[122] ﴿And wait; indeed, we are waiting.﴾

﴿And wait﴾ — that is, for the outcomes (al-'Awaqib). ﴿Indeed, we are waiting﴾ — that is, for what we were promised of victory (al-Fath). Allah has fulfilled His promise and given victory to His servant, so to Him alone is all praise.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 11, verse 123:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[123] ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter will be returned. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: nothing hidden from Him of what occurs within them is concealed from Him, and so your deeds are not concealed from Him. ﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾, meaning: the affair of the servants in the Hereafter, so He will recompense them for their deeds. In this is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) and a warning to the disbelievers of retribution against them. ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾, for He is sufficient for you. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, with the yā' (the third-person form, "they do") in the reading of the majority of reciters, in harmony with His saying: ﴿for those who do not believe﴾ [Hud: 121]. And in another reading with the tā' (the second-person form, "you do"), by way of giving precedence to the addressee, meaning: you and they. That is, He will recompense each according to what he deserves, and Allah knows best.
